reviews.title: Great tracker, mid system
reviews.text: I have used this system for calisthenics for nearly 10 years. That said, I find that the algorithm is not actually effective! By week 3 or 4, I cannot complete an entire set as-given, instead splitting their 5 sets into 9 or more. I also cannot do 100 push-ups. Even so, this system has helped me keep a routine, and that has maintained my fitness very well.

reviews.title: Gains start to become unrealistic around week 4
reviews.text: Starting around Week 4, the app will start expecting you to be able to do an extra 10 or more pushups with every workout. This feels unreasonable. I expect this is because the “100 continuous pushups in 6 weeks” is an unrealistic goal to begin with. Still, the set counter and rest timer work well and you will see gains. Just expect to fail certain workouts and retry them after a few days of rest.

reviews.title: Combo workout

reviews.title: Здравствуйте.
reviews.text:
Приветствую. Скажите, каким образом происходит адаптация программы под мой уровень? Когда в последнем подходе делаю больше, чем задумано планом на этот день — следующий день пересчитываться должен? У меня просто не пересчитывается, какой был план на следующий день — такой и остался, хоть в 20 раз больше запланированного сделаю в последнем подходе. Как это работает, можете объяснить?

В качестве предложения: сделайте пожалуйста возможность настроить перерыв между подходами вручную один раз и зафиксировать его, чтоб каждый раз не тапать.

reviews.title: If you follow the exercises, it does as promised
reviews.text:
Update: nothing I said below has changed, but if you haven’t updated your app in 2 years, you have NO business charging a recurring subscription. Period. The concept of software as a service is just that - a service. You released an app that is complete. So charge a price and be done with it. Knocked down three stars, this BS has to stop, it’s every app now.

This app works. Plain and simple. I started only being able to do 3 pushups (I know, embarrassing). In two weeks, I did 40. It breaks them into manageable chunks per session, so it almost tricks you into doing more than you realize. Another great thing is the free version has NO ads until after the workout, at which point you can just shut it off anyway. What a breath of fresh air. It has reminders to get started and timers during the workout for breaks in between sets (default about a minute). I haven’t tried the pro version, but if it is just more of this, I don’t see what not to like. Simple, not cluttered, an app that delivers exactly what it promises with no B.S. That is a RARE find in a mobile App Store.

reviews.title: Bad design
reviews.text: I have been using this app for a while and I even bought the “pro” version. However, I need to give it a bad rating because of a terribly bad design. You can create an account and have your data linked to your account, but you don’t need to. So far so good. The problem is that, if you create an account and log in, and then for whatever reason you are logged out (maybe an app update logs you out), your data is saved to your phone as a separate account and when you realise you have been logged out and log back in, the app does not recognise your data and you have separate records with no way to reconcile them.

reviews.title: Program just doesn’t work.
reviews.text: Quite simply, the program just doesn’t work. The whole idea is you gradually increase the push-ups you do until you can do 50 in one go on your 3rd day of the 6th week. Well, I’ve been stuck on week 5, day 1 for about 2 weeks now and haven’t been able to hit my mark. I’m able to do quite a few more pushups than I could before, which is why I’ve given it 2 stars, but their program just isn’t a guarantee.
